clue.text: Policeman getting very warm in Indian garment

indicators.note: in says the warm word sits inside the policeman

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
very warm means hot

explanation.surface: An officer overheats while wearing traditional Indian dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the loincloth wrapped round the waist worn by many men in India, so a garment from there.

clue.text: Deserter's caught in time, making mistakes

indicators.note: caught in says the deserter is trapped inside the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is someone who deserts a cause; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A runaway soldier is captured just in time, while blundering.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural for errors, especially a printed list of corrections in a book.

clue.text: Russian geneticist getting yokels upset about reproduction finally

indicators.note: about says the jumbled yokels go round the other letter
upset says the letters of yokels are knocked over into a new order
finally picks the closing letter of reproduction

explanation.surface: A Soviet scientist offends country folk with his views on breeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns YOKELS into LYSEKO, and 'about' wraps that round N, the last letter of 'reproduction'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trofim Lysenko was the Soviet biologist whose rejection of Mendelian heredity dominated Stalin-era science.

clue.text: Journalist having last slices of the sliced bread brought up

indicators.note: last slices of takes the end letter from each of the words the and sliced
in a down clue brought up says the bread word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: roti is an Indian flatbread

explanation.surface: A reporter gets the heel of the loaf served to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last slices of' gives E and D from 'the sliced'; 'brought up' reverses ROTI to ITOR beneath them.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a senior journalist who prepares and oversees what a newspaper publishes.

clue.text: Homeless creature lately seen wandering round about

indicators.note: round says the jumbled letters go round the word for about
wandering says the letters of lately stray into a new order

parts.note: CA is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A stray animal has recently been seen roaming the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley cat is a stray feline living on the streets with no owner's home.

clue.text: Be poised to tell tales about unruly child

indicators.note: about says the word for telling tales goes round the child

parts.note: to tell tales is to lie
a brat is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: Someone poised to report on a naughty youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: To librate is to balance or sway gently back and forth, as a body held in equilibrium does.

clue.text: Pia lazes around somewhere in Italy

indicators.note: around says the letters of Pia lazes are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman called Pia lounges about at some Italian spot.
explanation.definitionFit: La Spezia is a port city on the Ligurian coast in north-west Italy, so a place in that country.

clue.text: McKellen's first to abandon perfect stage role in Othello

indicators.note: to abandon says that letter leaves the insect word

parts.note: the imago is the final, fully developed stage of an insect

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of McKellen

explanation.surface: Ian McKellen quits a flawless production to take a part in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect stage' looks theatrical but is entomology: IMAGO loses M.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the scheming ensign in Shakespeare's Othello, a part McKellen himself has played.

clue.text: Badger a prince

definitions.meaning: to badger is to pester or harass

explanation.surface: A member of royalty is likened to a woodland animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to pester them persistently, and Harry is the younger son of King Charles.

clue.text: A country in the manner of Germany rejected a religious leader

indicators.note: rejected says the whole string is turned back to front

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa
a la, from French, means in the manner of
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A nation imitating Germany spurns a spiritual figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses AMALIALAD to give the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism.

clue.text: Boiler made of wood on purpose in Scotland

parts.note: teak is a hard timber
ettle is a Scots word for purpose or intent

explanation.surface: A heating vessel built from timber deliberately, north of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: A kettle for tea boils water, so it is a boiler in the plain sense of the word.

clue.text: Sort of furniture salesman getting run over

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A furniture seller gets knocked down by a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Repro furniture is reproduction furniture, modern copies of antique styles.

clue.text: Dad's Army private similar to one deserting during conflict

indicators.note: during says the shortened word sits within the conflict

parts.note: a conflict is a war

indicators.note: deserting says the one leaves the word for similar

parts.note: similar to means like
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A soldier in a wartime comedy resembles someone going AWOL mid-battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic British sitcom about the wartime Home Guard, a volunteer force of older men.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Joe Walker is the spiv of the Home Guard platoon in the BBC comedy Dad's Army.

clue.text: Nazi necktie modelled in film

indicators.note: modelled says the letters of Nazi necktie are shaped into something new

explanation.surface: A fascist's tie is worn on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles's 1941 drama about a press baron is often called the greatest movie ever made.

clue.text: Require Anne Reed to appear in regular instalments

indicators.note: in regular instalments picks every second letter of Anne Reed

explanation.surface: Anne Reed is called to turn up at set intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to require it; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Copy a card game

definitions.meaning: cribbage, often shortened, is a card game scored on a pegboard

explanation.definitionFit: Crib means to plagiarise, and is the short name for the card game cribbage.

clue.text: Something growing in orderly lines, it's said

indicators.note: it's said says the word for lines is heard, not spelt

parts.note: neat lines are rows

explanation.surface: A plant coming up in neat garden rows, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose is a flowering shrub, so a thing that grows; the definition is deliberately vague.

clue.text: Cantina in Star Wars, for example, that's sort of key

definitions.text: Cantina in Star Wars, for example
definitions.meaning: the Mos Eisley cantina is a drinking den in a sci-fi film, so a bar in space
the long bar at the bottom of a keyboard that types a gap

explanation.surface: A sci-fi film's alien bar is linked to some kind of key.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar in Star Wars is a bar in space, and the keyboard key making gaps between words has this name.

clue.text: Favourite thermoplastic polymer resin

definitions.meaning: polyethylene terephthalate, the plastic of drinks bottles, is abbreviated this way

explanation.definitionFit: A favourite is a pet, and the abbreviation for polyethylene terephthalate gives the same letters.

clue.text: Clown supporting 13 paying too much attention to detail

definitions.text: paying too much attention to detail

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting puts the clown below the other piece

parts.note: 13 across is a walker, and a ped is a pedestrian
an antic is an old word for a clown or buffoon

explanation.surface: A clown holding up a pedestrian who fusses over trifles.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantic describes someone overly concerned with minor rules and fine points.

clue.text: See 14
Somehow tries to take in races in passages that are fast

indicators.note: to take in says the jumbled letters enclose the races
somehow says the letters of tries are arranged in some other way

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy, motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to fit some racing into speedy sections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passages' suggests corridors, but this is a musical term; TT races are held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretti, plural of stretto, are passages in music, often at a faster tempo, where entries overlap closely.

clue.text: Italian maestro getting back of old car entangled with front of supermarket

parts.note: the Viva was a Vauxhall car of the 1960s and 70s

indicators.note: entangled with front of says the car's last letter and the store's first letter merge, so only one is written

parts.note: Aldi is a discount supermarket chain

explanation.surface: A shopping trip goes wrong as a vintage car runs into a store's entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting back of' points to the final A of VIVA; it overlaps the opening A of ALDI, giving VIV-A-LDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Vivaldi was the Venetian Baroque composer of The Four Seasons.

clue.text: Severely criticised for being the biggest night owl, figuratively

definitions.text: being the biggest night owl, figuratively
definitions.meaning: the person staying up latest is last to bed, pictured as the word last sitting inside bed

explanation.surface: A late-night reveller gets a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a picture: LAST put into BED gives B-LAST-ED, as the biggest night owl is the last one into bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To be blasted is to be attacked harshly in words, as a critic savages a show.

clue.text: Yorkshire town having intelligence to cover back of Church Times

indicators.note: to cover says the wit word surrounds that letter

parts.note: wit is intelligence or sharpness of mind

indicators.note: back of picks the closing letter of Church

parts.note: by means times, as in four by three

explanation.surface: A northern town's intelligent paper covers the Church Times.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church Times is a real Anglican weekly paper, but here it splits: 'back of Church' is H and 'Times' is BY.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitby is a seaside town on the North Yorkshire coast famous for its abbey and Dracula.

clue.text: Did Father Crilly use to be drunk?

parts.note: was is the past of be, what something used to be
Father Ted Crilly is the hapless priest in the Irish sitcom Father Ted

explanation.surface: A question about whether a TV priest was once a drinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted is a 1990s sitcom about three priests on an Irish island; read the clue as 'Father Crilly was Ted' for the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasted is slang for very intoxicated, as is drunk.

clue.text: Get lost for example in Ilium, say

indicators.note: in says the abbreviation sits inside the bone

parts.note: the ilium is the large upper bone of the pelvis, so an example of a bone
eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: An order to leave, as might be shouted in ancient Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ilium is the Latin name for Troy, which tempts a classical reading; here it is the hip bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone is an old-fashioned command to go away, like the modern dismissive phrase.

clue.text: Horny creature very tastelessly sent up in part

indicators.note: sent up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lustful beast is mocked in very poor taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a goat-horned woodland spirit of Greek myth known for lust, so horny in both senses.

clue.text: Scandalous Christine's unable to finish university

indicators.note: unable to finish says the surname loses its closing letter

parts.note: Christine Keeler was the model at the centre of the 1963 Profumo scandal; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A notorious woman can't complete her degree.
explanation.walkthrough: The Profumo affair was a British political sex scandal that brought down a government minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Keele University is a campus institution in Staffordshire, England.

clue.text: Scottish channel featuring Australian songbird (not current)

indicators.note: not says the current letter is removed from the singer's name

parts.note: Kylie Minogue is an Australian pop singer
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A Scottish TV station showcases an Aussie pop star, minus electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A kyle is a narrow strait of water in Scotland, as in the Kyle of Lochalsh.

clue.text: Foolishly lost again in yearning for the past

indicators.note: foolishly says the letters of lost again are arranged in a silly new order

explanation.surface: Someone stupidly gets lost once more while pining for old times.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental longing for an earlier time.

clue.text: Most stupid, at any rate, in the US

definitions.meaning: split into two words, ... means having the least sense

definitions.text: at any rate, in the US
definitions.meaning: an American dialect word meaning at least or in any case

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it describes the dimmest person; as one word it is American for anyway or at least.

clue.text: Boy providing news throughout 24 hours

indicators.note: throughout says the news letters run through the middle of the day

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours
N is short for new, and doubled it stands for news, the plural

explanation.surface: A lad delivers bulletins around the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Danny is a common boy's name, a familiar form of Daniel.
